note: Gap pass for the life_stage lens, re-grounded on 2026-09-27 with fresh web searches (the first version reused URLs from sibling files without searching). Every 'where' URL and every price URL below appeared in a search result during the re-grounding task (seen_via: search). Prices are copied exactly from the search-result text; the URL on each step is the result page that text is attributed to. Direct page fetches are blocked by the network, so no price was checked on the page itself; Stage 2 must verify each one. reddit.com is not reachable by the search tool, so no Reddit place is listed even where the room also gathers there. Sizes are estimates; measured supersets are cited inside the reasoning.

rooms.name: Investment banking associates and VPs (4 to 10 years in) planning to leave banking
rooms.who: Mid-career bankers who have done the analyst years and one or two promotions. They are 28 to 38, often married or about to be, and tired of the hours. In the next 1 to 3 years they want to move to corporate development, a startup finance role, a family office, a small fund, an MBA, or their own business. Their gap is that recruiting at this level is quiet and unstructured: no on-cycle, no headhunter calendar, and their skills are wide but their story is unclear. Forum threads say associates find exits harder than analysts, and VPs are 'too junior to have a book of clients, too expensive to be an execution monkey'.

Wall Street Oasis thread: Best VP exits

rooms.who_pays: The banker, from a high salary and bonus. Some employers pay for an MBA or a management course.

size.unit: associates and VPs at investment banks worldwide who are actively planning an exit in a given year
size.reasoning: No direct count was seen. Bulge-bracket, elite-boutique and mid-market banks together employ on the order of 100,000 front-office bankers worldwide; associates and VPs are roughly a third, and the exit threads above show a large minority looking at any time. For churn context, a layoff tracker counts 74,855 finance and banking jobs cut in 2026 to 2 September [measured, superset, https://layoffhedge.com/industry/finance-layoffs-2026]. Treat the number as a rough order of magnitude.

ladder.problem: Pick the exit and rebuild the story: interview prep for the target role (the price seen is WSO's investment banking interview course; corporate development and fund interviews reuse the same technicals)
Refresh modelling for a buy-side or corporate development test after years of pitch work
Coaching by the hour on the pivot story and the search
The MBA route as a reset: GMAT registration (test centre)
Admissions consulting for a multi-school MBA application (comprehensive package)
ladder.price_text: $6,950 for 1 school, $8,950 for 2 schools, and $10,950 for 3 schools

ladder.problem: The own-business route: price fractional CFO work to sell (what companies pay a fractional CFO is the benchmark)

rooms.reasoning: One life stage with a shared, dated pressure (promotion or leave; bonus timing; a family forming) and named forum threads where exactly these people post. The founder's warmest path is current and former banking colleagues, and corporate finance is a strong depth domain. Existing rooms cover analysts recruiting for PE and consultants moving into finance; nobody covers mid-level bankers moving out.

rooms.name: Mid-career professionals leaving a corporate job to buy a small business (self-funded searchers)
rooms.who: People in their 30s and 40s, many from banking, consulting or corporate finance, who want to own and run a company rather than start one. Over 12 to 24 months they search listings for a business worth $0.5M to $10M, value it, get a loan, close, and then run it. Most have never bought anything bigger than a house and are afraid of overpaying or buying a business that depends on its owner. Since June 2025 the SBA rules require a 10% equity injection, with at least 5% in non-borrowed cash, which raises the stakes of the first deal.

where.name: Searchfunder, the online community for search funds and self-funded searchers (over 10,000 members including operators, investors, lenders and brokers)

rooms.who_pays: The buyer, from savings and later from the business itself. An SBA 7(a) or bank loan pays most of the purchase price; the buyer must put in at least 10% of total project cost.

size.unit: active individual buyers of small businesses in the US in a year
size.reasoning: Searchfunder reports over 10,000 members, but that includes investors, brokers, lawyers and accountants as well as searchers [measured, superset, https://searchfunder.com/post/faq]. BizBuySell says it is visited over 4 million times a month by potential buyers and has facilitated over 200,000 sales in total [measured, superset, https://www.bizbuysell.com/]. Individual buyers of businesses above $0.5M are one slice of that; tens of thousands a year is a conservative order of magnitude. Other countries add to it.

ladder.problem: Learn how small deals work and choose a search path (Searchfunder is a paid subscription with monthly, annual and lifetime tiers; the price was not shown in results)
Fund the deal: the SBA 7(a) equity injection the buyer must find
ladder.price_text: minimum equity injection of 10% of total project costs

ladder.problem: Value the target for the lender (an independent, SBA-format valuation)
Check the seller's numbers: a quality of earnings report
Negotiate the deal: the broker's commission is built into the price
ladder.price_text: 8 to 12 percent of the sale price for businesses under about $1 million

ladder.problem: Sign: a lawyer drafts the asset purchase agreement (licensed partner)
Run it after closing: bookkeeping, cash planning and a fractional CFO
Grow it without hiring: an AI voice agent to answer every call (platform base fee)

rooms.reasoning: A clear life stage (the year or two between quitting and closing) with big, sequential paid problems and a dedicated community (Searchfunder) where the same people post. The run already has the sellers (retiring owners) and the brokers, but not the buyers. The founder's valuation and deal-document depth is strong, and many searchers come from his banking and PE network. Step 8 touches TinyAI.

rooms.name: First-year students at IIMs, ISB and other top Indian B-schools preparing for finance and consulting summer placements
rooms.who: Students who just joined a two-year MBA at an IIM, XLRI, FMS or similar, or the one-year ISB programme. Within 8 to 12 weeks of arriving they face summer placement week (IIM Bangalore's ran 13 to 18 October 2025), where banks, PE funds and consulting firms interview on day zero and day one. They must learn valuation, guesstimates and case interviews from scratch while carrying a full course load and a large loan. Final placements repeat the cycle a year later.

rooms.who_pays: The student, mostly on an education loan, sometimes with parents' money. The fee already committed makes a good placement feel non-negotiable.

size.unit: students joining the IIMs, ISB and the top ten other Indian B-schools each year
size.reasoning: IIM Bangalore alone placed 601 first-year students in summer placements 2026, described as the largest batch across all IIMs [measured, https://insideiim.com/iim-bangalore-concludes-summer-placements-2026-with-record-46-consulting-offers-largest-batch-among-all-iims-placed-in-six-days]. Twenty-one IIMs at a few hundred each, ISB at roughly 900, and the next tier of schools together give about 8,000 a year entering the schools where finance and consulting firms recruit. Not every student targets those firms, but most sit the prep.

ladder.problem: Fund the programme before joining: the total fee at a top IIM (PGP 2025-27, the latest published)
Education loan for the fee (SBI rate for IIM-A students)
Case interview coaching from ex-consultants before summer placement week
Finance technicals for bank and PE interviews: an interview guide and question bank
Financial modelling before the summer internship and final placements
Signal finance intent with CFA Level I registration (early registration)
If placements miss: a placement-linked investment banking operations programme

rooms.reasoning: The run has CAT aspirants (before admission) and US MBA students switching into banking, but not the Indian B-school cohort itself, whose placement process is its own fixed-date event with its own prep guides on InsideIIM. Indian investment banking teams are full of IIM and ISB alumni, so the founder's colleague network reaches them warmly, and corporate finance and case interviews are ledger depth domains.

rooms.name: Ex-bankers and ex-consultants in their first year as the first finance hire at a funded startup
rooms.who: People 3 to 8 years into banking, consulting or Big 4 who just joined a seed-to-Series-B startup as head of finance, finance lead or chief of staff for finance. They are the only finance person. In their first year they must build the fundraising model and data room, fix the books, set up board reporting, run the next round's diligence, and hire the first analyst, none of which they have done before. Investor guides say post-Series A boards expect board-ready financials, monthly reporting packages and variance analysis from this hire.

rooms.who_pays: The startup pays for tools, advisers and outsourced finance; the person pays for their own courses and coaching.

size.unit: people worldwide who start as the first finance hire at a funded startup in a year
size.reasoning: The Startup CFO community counts 1,400 finance leaders [measured, superset of stages, https://startupcfo.tech/]. Data from 218 startups says most make the first full-time finance hire in the 30 to 50 employee range [measured, https://www.getaleph.com/blog/finance-team-structure]. A few thousand startups reach that size each year in the US alone; with India, Europe and Southeast Asia added, low tens of thousands a year is a reasonable order of magnitude.

ladder.problem: Build the fundraising deck and model for the next round (seed-stage deck design average)
Decide what to outsource: the fractional CFO benchmark they must beat or buy
Get deal-ready for the round: three-statement and DCF modelling refresher
Run the round: what a fundraising adviser charges if they cannot do it alone
Annual compliance of the entity they now own: registered agent after year one (US example)
Cut cost centres they now own: AI voice agents for support and sales calls (platform base fee)
Grow into CFO: hire and manage the first analyst (new-manager training)

rooms.reasoning: A one-year life stage with a fixed sequence of first-time tasks (model, books, board pack, next round) and dedicated communities (Startup CFO, CFO Connect) that name this person as their member. The founder's colleagues who left banking for startups are a direct warm path, and valuation, deal documents and investor reporting are strong depth. FP&A analysts (profession lens) and first-time founders are already listed; the first finance hire between them is not. Confidence is moderate now that the communities are seen directly.
